newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico cautiously welcomes Cuba law suspension.
newsitem.headline: Mexico cautiously welcomes Cuba law suspension.

text.p: Mexico on Friday was cautiously upbeat about U.S. President Bill Clinton's suspension of a law imposing sanctions on Communist-ruled Cuba but reiterated the law should be scrapped.

"The Mexican government recognizes that the decision of President Clinton marks an effort to take into account the opinion of the international community," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement published by state news agency Notimex.

Mexico has been one of the loudest opponents of the Helms-Burton act that would allow Americans to sue foreigners with certain investments in Cuba. Mexican firms have burgeoning business interests on the Caribbean island.
"The Mexican government reaffirms the need to resolve any international differences via open and respectful dialogue, not via unilateral and confrontational methods," it said.

On Friday, Clinton said he would continue a six-month suspension of the bill for a further half year, after receiving assurances from its opponents, including Canada and the European Commission, that they were working to help bring democracy to Cuba.
